clue.text: Animal food one found in the smithy

indicators.note: one thing found in another sits inside it, so this phrase puts the first piece within the second

parts.note: a smithy is a blacksmith's workshop, a forge
one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A farmhand discovers fodder lying about in the blacksmith's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Forage is fodder such as hay or grass fed to horses and cattle.

parts.note: Fore! is the golfer's shouted warning to watch out
a lock is a fastening on a door

explanation.surface: Someone is warned to take care when pinning up hair.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the warning cry on a golf course, telling people nearby to be careful of the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A forelock is the lock of hair growing just above the forehead.

clue.text: Faith left one in the area

indicators.note: the letters for left and one are placed inside the word for area

parts.note: a region is an area
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A believer left behind one faith that dominated the district.
explanation.definitionFit: A religion is a faith, a system of belief and worship.

clue.text: Blow a bit of soot through a crevice

indicators.note: the gap runs through, around, the small piece of soot, so one sits within the other

parts.note: a crevice is a gap or crack

indicators.note: only a small bit of the word is used, its first letter

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep blows a speck of soot out through a crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' works as a container: the crack runs right round the speck. 'Blow' here is a noun or verb of breathing, not a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to blow, pant or catch one's breath sharply.

parts.note: egg is old military slang for a bomb or mine
a plant is an industrial factory

explanation.surface: A munitions works is discussed as if it were a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bomb factory; in fact 'Bomb' gives EGG and 'factory' gives PLANT, and the plant that grows aubergines is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The eggplant (aubergine) is the plant on which that purple vegetable grows.

parts.note: to gain is to get

indicators.note: without its end, the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: the name Bob
rough, like a sea, means agitated

explanation.surface: A painter finds a man called Bob getting more and more worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' removes the last B from BOB, leaving BO. Thomas Gainsborough was an 18th-century English portrait and landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsborough is a famous English painter, so an example of an artist.

indicators.note: the word reads identically whether read left to right or right to left

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone is told to check in both directions before crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ways' says the answer is a palindrome; 'Look both ways' is the road-safety instruction that disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to take a quick look.

clue.text: Stir up a backwash on end of run

parts.note: the wake of a ship is its backwash

indicators.note: the end of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A boat leaves a backwash behind as it finishes a run.
explanation.definitionFit: To awaken is to rouse or stir someone up.

indicators.note: the word for attempt holds, keeps, the word for close within it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stay near the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the definition, as in 'the in thing': fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in is fashionable, the latest style.

clue.text: Old priest's in Haiti for enjoyment

indicators.note: the old priest's letters go inside the code for Haiti

parts.note: RH, for Republique d'Haiti, is Haiti's international vehicle registration code
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel; with the 's he gives ELIS

explanation.surface: A biblical priest is said to be enjoying himself in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: RH is Haiti's vehicle code (Republique d'Haiti), not a crossword staple; the possessive on 'priest's' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish is keen enjoyment or zest.

parts.note: aired means broadcast or made public
ale is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: A drink is advertised for a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire.

clue.text: Fear hooter is ill-fitted to make lots of noise

indicators.note: something badly fitted together is assembled wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car horn badly installed would make a frightful din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-fitted' rearranges FEARHOOTERIS into the answer; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise the roof is an idiom for making a great deal of noise, cheering or shouting.

indicators.note: without its heart, the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to lunge is to leap or thrust forward

explanation.surface: A tobogganist pushes off with a cold-blooded jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' removes N, the middle letter, from LUNGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A luge is a small racing sled ridden feet first, a kind of toboggan.

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the time word

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A bridesmaid is right on time for the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower girl' wants to be a bridesmaid; here it means a girl with a flower's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisy is both a common flower and a girl's name.

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the word for garden

parts.note: a flower bed is a garden plot
one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone drops something somewhere in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead is a small drop of liquid, as of sweat.

definitions.meaning: a runner is a plant's new growth, a sprout

explanation.surface: Someone talks about how fast an athlete is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete; it is a botanical runner, a new stem.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoot means both to dash quickly and a new growth from a plant.

clue.text: American riding round rail way annex

indicators.note: the word for riding goes round the railway letter

parts.note: up means riding, as a jockey is up on a horse
R is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: An American on a train trip around the line takes over territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail way' is printed split but reads as railway, abbreviated R.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize or take over, as one might annex land.

clue.text: School Esther reformed becomes a model

indicators.note: something reformed is made over in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl named Esther, transformed by her school, turns into a model pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges SCHOOLESTHER; 'becomes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse is someone who loves fashion and shows off clothes, like a model.

clue.text: Person in poem is a painter

indicators.note: the person word goes inside the poem word

parts.note: verse is poetry, a poem
one is a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: A character in a poem turns out to be an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Paolo Veronese was a 16th-century Venetian painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronese is a Renaissance Italian painter, so an example of a painter.

indicators.note: one thing during another sits within it, so the point goes inside the proposal

parts.note: an offer is a proposal
the point of something is its end or tip

explanation.surface: A crook makes a point while a deal is being proposed.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is a lawbreaker, someone who commits a crime.

definitions.meaning: homespun means homemade, done by amateurs
harried employees might snap back telling their boss to handle it personally

explanation.surface: Weary employees snap back at a demanding boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes amateur home handiwork and is also a curt reply telling someone to handle it alone.

clue.text: In favour of suitable inter est

parts.note: pro means in favour of
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: Someone backs a suitable investment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is printed split as 'inter est': read it as interest, in the sense of financial gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is financial gain, the return on money, as interest is.

indicators.note: the dishonour word holds the royal letter tightly inside

parts.note: a stain is a mark of dishonour
R stands for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: Scandal takes hold of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a line of descent or breed, a family stock.

indicators.note: the broadcaster's initials hold the letter inside them

parts.note: RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster

explanation.surface: Ireland's television keeps up a certain quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate is a standard or level, as in first-rate.

definitions.meaning: spoken, Winnie gives the sound of whinny, a horse's call
a noise made by an animal

explanation.surface: Someone named Winnie heard a noise from an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works by sound: Winnie said out loud is whinny, which means the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the whinnying cry of a horse.

indicators.note: the female animal grabs and holds the coin letter inside

parts.note: a doe is a female deer or rabbit
bob is old British slang for a shilling, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: A female animal grabs Bob's medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a shilling in pre-decimal British money, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose is a prescribed quantity of medicine.

definitions.meaning: someone who ties or fastens things
a bank is a row or ..., as of seats or oars

explanation.surface: Someone fastens a boat to the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one who ties and also a row or level in a series.

parts.note: to vet is to check
O is a blood group

explanation.surface: A lab rejects a sample after checking its blood type.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto is to reject or forbid formally.

clue.text: Trainee tucking into quiche that's smoother

indicators.note: the trainee goes inside, tucks into, the dish

parts.note: a quiche is a savoury flan
a tiro is a beginner or novice

explanation.surface: An apprentice is eating a quiche.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating, but signals one piece put inside another; 'Trainee' is the less common spelling tiro (tyro).
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron is an old-fashioned iron heated on a stove, used to smooth clothes.

clue.text: Celebrity went ahead without the facts

indicators.note: here meaning outside, so the went-ahead word wraps round the facts

parts.note: led means went in front
gen is British slang for information, the facts

explanation.surface: A famous person pressed on without checking the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a very famous person, a star.

clue.text: Fine tree destroyed in holiday destination

indicators.note: a thing destroyed is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fine tree is ruined at a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges FINETREE; Tenerife is the largest of the Spanish Canary Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife is a popular holiday island, an example of a resort.

parts.note: a do is a party
gear is clothing

explanation.surface: Party outfits are folded.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-ear is a folded-down corner of a page.
